lines: Ever wonder why your belly growls like a tiny thunderstorm?

beats.text: The rumble is just gas and fluid sliding through your intestines as they contract.
lines: The rumble is just gas and fluid sliding through your intestines as they contract.
Peristalsis pushes the mixture along, and the moving gas creates the gurgle.

beats.text: When the stomach is empty, the space amplifies the noise, so growls are louder.
lines: When the stomach is empty, the space amplifies the noise, so growls are louder.
That’s why you hear it strongest right before a meal.
Every 90 to 230 minutes, a fasting wave called the migrating motor complex sweeps the gut, creating the classic rumble.
It also helps clear leftover food and bacteria between meals.

beats.text: Swallowed air while talking or drinking makes bubbles that add to the rumble.
lines: Swallowed air while talking or drinking makes bubbles that add to the rumble.
Carbonated drinks can make the effect even louder.
Try sipping water and notice the silence right after.

sources.claim: Stomach rumble is produced by movement of gas and fluid through the intestines as they contract.
Louder rumbles occur when the stomach is empty; empty space amplifies the sound.
The migrating motor complex occurs every 90–230 minutes during fasting and causes rumbling.
Swallowed air while talking, eating, or drinking creates bubbles that add to stomach noises.

youtube.title: Why does your stomach growl? 🤔
youtube.description: Find out what really makes your belly rumble, when it happens, and how to quiet it.
